rational_vs_algebraic_grade_scope_audit.unique_real_solution_formula: For prime p and integer k >= 1, the unique real K solving p^k = tau^K is K = k log(p) / log(tau).
rational_vs_algebraic_grade_scope_audit.rational_exclusion_status: PROVED_IRRATIONAL_BY_LINDEMANN: K not in Q. If K = a/b is nonzero rational (a in Z \ {0}, b in Z_{>=1}), clearing the rational exponent yields tau^{|a|} - p^{k b} = 0 (or p^{k b} tau^{|a|} - 1 = 0), a nonzero polynomial over Q satisfied by tau = 2*pi, contradicting the transcendence of tau (Lindemann 1882).
rational_vs_algebraic_grade_scope_audit.algebraic_irrational_vs_transcendental_s: OPEN_UNESTABLISHED: Rational exclusion K not in Q does NOT determine whether K = k log(p) / log(tau) is algebraic irrational (K in A_R \ Q) or transcendental (K not in A_R).
rational_vs_algebraic_grade_scope_audit.why_cited_theorems_do_not_exclude_algebr: Gelfond-Schneider requires an algebraic base alpha in Q_bar \ {0, 1} in alpha^beta (whereas the base tau = 2*pi in tau^K is transcendental); Lindemann-Weierstrass requires algebraic exponents in e^alpha and does not turn K log(tau) into an algebraic exponent when K in A_R \ {0}.
rational_vs_algebraic_grade_scope_audit.tc_admissibility_consequence: Prime-power scales p^k and dyadic scales 2^j do not automatically define admissible algebraic tau-grade shifts; no admissibility or universal inadmissibility is assumed for an irrational K.
